title: Aether Security World - Oracle Output v0.1
description: The deterministic verdict for one episode. REVISION 1: `required_evidence[].decision_fact` now carries the canonical fact key the oracle computed the closure over, so 'what the decision needed' has exactly one owner (the oracle) and is directly comparable with evidence.asserts_ref. `skipped_invariants` records out-of-scope invariants so that satisfied ∪ violated ∪ skipped == all invariants is checkable. `evidence_view_id` is redefined as sha256(world_id, action_id, visible evidence) - the old definition (hash of the visible set alone) made an unsatisfiable promise, because observable_decision is a function of (world, action, evidence view), not of the evidence view alone.

world_truth.$comment: Computed over the FULL world state. REVISION 1 aggregation rule: attack iff (a) a NON-default policy rule denied the action, or (b) at least one invariant was violated. Severity no longer participates - it is an author-writable enum and using it handed label authority to whoever wrote the world. ATTACK_CATEGORIES is engine-private and equals the full category list: a violated security invariant is an attack by definition.

observable_decision.$comment: Computed over the VISIBLE evidence only, using the established fact values rather than world truth. When a decision-critical fact cannot be established from evidence in TRUSTED_ESTABLISHES = {trusted, semi_trusted}, this is insufficient_evidence even if world_truth is attack. 'unauthorized' (default-deny only, no invariant violated) stays observable as unauthorized.

skipped_invariants.$comment: REVISION 1: invariants out of scope for this action's operation, or in scope but with an unbound subject. Recorded, never silently dropped and never counted as satisfied. Assertion: violated ∪ satisfied ∪ skipped == every invariant id in the world.

required_evidence.description: Every evidence item the computed decision closure needed, keyed by the canonical fact key. `decision_fact` is what makes this comparable with evidence.asserts_ref.

decision_fact.$comment: REVISION 2: the canonical ID-view path BNF (design §4.3) - the same pattern as evidence.asserts_ref, so the two are byte-comparable (D3). One path grammar, one notation (task A3).

asserts_ref.$comment: REVISION 2: the canonical ID-view path BNF (design §4.3) - identical to evidence.schema.json and episode.schema.json evidence_observation (task A3).

decision_fact.$comment: REVISION 2: the canonical ID-view path BNF (design §4.3), identical to required_evidence[].decision_fact above (task A3).

decision_trace.description: Ordered machine execution record of the rule evaluation that produced the verdicts. Each entry names the rule, the operands and the result. Reproducible by re-running the same rules; contains no natural-language reasoning. `evidence.sufficiency` operands carry `consulted_facts`: the refs actually read during evaluation (short-circuited branches excluded).

evidence_view_id.$comment: REVISION 1: sha256 over (world_id, action_id, canonical visible evidence set). The determinism guarantee is 'same (world, action, evidence view) => same output', NOT 'same evidence view => same output' - two worlds can share a visible evidence set and still differ.
